title: Forensic Evidence Garden — PRD exploration
content:
Overview

This doc captures an exploratory PRD for a compact, queryable "Forensic Evidence Garden" intended for private deployments (customer-managed networking / VPC). The goal is to provide teams and security reviewers with a pragmatic way to collect, index, and retrieve minimal forensic artifacts tied to VPC configuration changes, operator approvals, and runtime network events. Unlike large monolithic audit dumps, the Garden is a set of tiny, strongly-typed evidence shards that can be assembled on-demand into a compliance-grade package.

Why this exists (problem statement)
- Customers running Redwood Private want concise, legally defensible evidence packages for: change approvals, emergency rollbacks, and post-incident investigations.
- Full-fidelity packet- or syslog-level archives are expensive to store and difficult to search; customers prefer small, queryable proof bundles that show intent, authorization, and observable effects.
- Current proposals in the private-deployments space mix long retention, heavy telemetry, or operator-led evidence capture workflows — we need a lightweight, automation-friendly model that fits constrained operator budgets and privacy requirements.

Design thesis and guiding principles
1) Minimalism: capture only the smallest authoritative facts that prove an action and its observable consequence (e.g., signed approval token, pre/post routing snapshot diff hash, and a short telemetry fingerprint).
2) Composability: evidence shards are first-class artifacts (JSON lines) that can be composed into bundles for audits or incidents.
3) Verifiability: each shard carries a cryptographic signature or HMAC (customer KMS/HSM integration optional) so recipients can prove provenance.
4) Privacy-aware: default retention is short; customers can opt-in to longer retention windows for legal or compliance reasons.
5) Queryability: searchable indexes (time-bound, tag-bound) to quickly assemble relevant shards; no full-text indexing of raw packet content.

Scope (what this PRD covers)
- Schema definition for evidence shards (types, required fields).
- API contract for capturing and querying shards from operator or control-plane events.
- UX for the Console: evidence bundle builder and compact audit cards (low-fidelity).
- Approval gate integration: how evidence is attached to approval flows and rollback triggers.
- Retention & export policies with compliance metadata mapping (SOC2/GDPR/Roles).

Out of scope (for this iteration)
- Full packet capture storage or SIEM integration beyond simple forward hooks.
- Deep forensic tooling (timeline reconstruction beyond assembling shards).
- Operator training materials — will come later after prototyping.

Evidence shard schema (high level)
- shard_id (uuid, required)
- shard_type (enum: approval, snapshot, telemetry_fingerprint, config_diff, operator_comment, rollback_trigger)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- generated_by (string: service/component id)
- references (list of shard_ids; minimal)
- subject (string: short descriptor e.g., vpc:proj-a-subnet-3)
- payload_summary (short human-readable string, <250 chars)
- payload_hash (sha256 hex)
- signature (base64) OR hmac_id (if using customer HSM/KMS: key id)
- retention_ttl_days (int as string for now; UI mapping)
- compliance_tags (list of strings)

Notes on schema choices
- shards are intentionally small; full payloads are optional and can be stored encrypted in customer object storage and referenced by shard payload_hash + locator (signed URL).
- signature semantics: for hosted control-plane we sign with Redwood entry key; for private deployments customers can configure KMS to sign/hmac so proof bundles are verifiable by auditors.

API contracts (capture & query)
1) POST /evidence/shards - capture a shard (idempotent by shard_id). Body: flat JSON with fields above plus optional payload_locator. Returns 201/409.
2) GET /evidence/shards?from=...&to=...&subject=...&type=...&tag=... - paginated listing (cursor-based).
3) GET /evidence/bundles?bundle_id=... - retrieve assembled bundle (bundle is a signed manifest referencing shards + optionally zipped encrypted payloads).
4) POST /evidence/bundles/assemble - server-side assembly request; returns a bundle_id when ready with status polling.

Query semantics and performance guidance
- Typical assembly window should be < 10s for small bundles (<50 shards).
- Index by timestamp, subject, and primary compliance_tags. Full-text search is intentionally absent to limit PII exposure.
- Pagination default: 200 shards per page; default retention index partitioning by week.

Approval gate integration patterns
- Synchronous attach: when an approval is granted in the UI, the approval shard is created and attached to the approval object. This shard contains approver id, roles, decision, and the signed approval token.
- Preflight evidence: pre-change snapshot shard(s) are captured immediately before the change; post-change snapshot captured after success/failure. A change bundle comprises the approval shard + pre/post snapshots + optional telemetry_fingerprint(s).
- Rollback trigger: pre-registered rollback shards embed a small automatable script or operator contact if manual rollback is required. Rollback shards may be configured with elevated retention.

Console UX sketch (high level)
- Evidence timeline card (compact): shows a short sequence: approval → pre-snapshot → apply → post-snapshot → telemetry-fingerprint → bundle link. Each entry surfaces a one-line summary and quick-verify icon (signed/verified).
- Bundle builder: filter by subject/time/tags, preview shard summaries, create export (signed bundle) with configurable TTL on the signed URL.
- Compliance view: map bundles to compliance frameworks (SOC2 section, GDPR data subject note) via tags.

Retention and cost model
- Defaults: approval shards = 365 days; snapshot shards = 30 days; telemetry_fingerprint = 7 days; operator_comment = 90 days. Customers can override.
- Cost optimization: payloads (large diffs) should be stored in customer S3/GCS/Swift with only locators in Redwood shards for private deployments. Hosted control-plane may offer optional encrypted archive for an add-on.

Security, KMS, and privacy considerations
- All shards and payload locators must be access-controlled by tenant-scoped permissions.
- Integrations: support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Vault HSM for signature/hmac. Provide fallback: Redwood-managed signing for test/sandbox tenants.
- Redact PII in payload_summary; full payloads should be stored encrypted and accessible only to roles with approval to view.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
1) Schema and API endpoints implemented + unit tests.
2) Console evidence timeline card + bundle builder prototype.
3) Ability to assemble and download a signed bundle with at least: approval shard, pre-snapshot, post-snapshot, telemetry_fingerprint.
4) KMS HMAC signing integration for at least one customer-managed KMS provider (AWS KMS).
5) Performance: assemble 50 shards into bundle within 15s for 95th percentile.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (spikes): prototype shard schema, simple POST/GET endpoints, in-console timeline component (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (pilot): support for customer-managed KMS signing, retention overrides, and bundle export (4 weeks); onboard 2 pilot customers.
- Phase 2 (GA): hardened APIs, role-based access control checks, export audit logs; docs and runbook (6 weeks).

Open questions / trade-offs
- How much fidelity should a snapshot contain? Full route table vs. compact diff? Recommend compact diffs by default with an opt-in for full snapshot stored off-platform.
- Query privacy: customers may want full text search inside payloads; that conflicts with our privacy posture. Evaluate a redaction pipeline before search.
- Legal hold: how do we handle court-ordered holds that exceed standard TTLs? Need legal + compliance flow and a manual override API.

Next steps (immediate)
- Align with SRE and infra on index partitioning and expected storage pattern for shards.
- Draft the technical proto schema and share with Applied ML (telemetry fingerprinting spec).
- Spin up a tiny prototype service that accepts shards and returns a minimal bundle; demo to Solutions Eng.

Appendix: short example shard (human readable)
- shard_id: "b6f4c8a2-8c1d-4d43-b5e6-1e7f8eea12ab"
- shard_type: "approval"
- timestamp_utc: "2025-02-28T18:12:22Z"
- generated_by: "console-approval-service"
- subject: "vpc:acme-prod-subnet-3"
- payload_summary: "Ops lead approved egress rule change to allow 10.2.3.0/24 on port 443"
- payload_hash: "sha256:3a7b..."
- signature: "base64:MEUCIQD..."
- retention_ttl_days: "365"
